intro.text: This is Nagaland, all steep green hills, in the eastern corner of India. Seventeen big tribes live up here, and each one has its own language, its own clothes and its own customs. Assam lies below, on the flat. The main town is Kohima.

animal.text: The mithun is a huge black cattle beast with white legs, like socks. Its horns do not curl up; they go straight out sideways. It lives half wild in the forest.

food.text: Smoked pork is cooked here with axone, which is soya beans left in the warm until they go soft and very strong-smelling. Axone means, more or less, deep smell.

festival.text: Sekrenyi is a festival for washing clean. On the first morning people sprinkle themselves with a few drops of rice water from a pot, and then the village starts again.

hello.text: No one language works for everybody here. So in the markets people made a new one, Nagamese, out of bits of all of them. Anything written down is written in English.

line.text: This is Dzukou Valley. The floor of this valley looks like it has been covered in green velvet, rolling away in soft humps. It is not grass. It is bamboo: a dwarf sort that stays low, packed so tightly together that from up on the ridge it looks smooth.

This is the Naga Log Drum. One whole tree, hollowed out until several men can sit inside it in a row. It takes months of carving, out in the forest, and then every man in the village comes to drag it home. Beaten in the right pattern, it says a message the whole valley knows.

This is Khonoma. The hillsides round this village are cut into flat green steps, one under another, all the way down. That way rice can grow on a slope you could hardly stand up on. The village has stopped all hunting inside a piece of its own hills.

About a million little falcons come down on this lake in October. They have flown from Siberia, and they are going on to Africa, and this is where they stop to eat and sleep. The sky goes speckled with them and every wire has a row sitting on it.

This is Shilloi Lake. This is the biggest natural lake in Nagaland, lying in a hollow with pine trees all round it. Its older name is Lutsam, which means, simply, the place where the water collects. On a still day the pines stand upside down in it.
